title: Add the camera measurement
summary: Give each camera tag solution to the pose estimator, then see how close the estimate gets.

say.never:
`LocalizationSubsystem` already asks MW-Lib's proxy server for the camera **tag solutions** (a tag solution is the robot's position worked out from the AprilTags a camera can see) and loops over the new, sensible ones (it drops the wild ones). Nothing hands them to the pose estimator yet, so the estimate is just odometry, which slowly drifts.

You will do three things: 1) add one call that gives each solution to the estimator, 2) choose how much to trust the cameras, 3) drive around in the simulator and watch the estimate lock onto the real position.

You are done when the estimate stays within 6 centimeters and 1 degree of the true position after you stop.
say.bit: The tag solutions are collected but never given to the estimator. You will add one call, choose the trust, then watch the error in AdvantageScope shrink.

say.never:
`addVisionMeasurement(...)` takes three things, in this order.

1) **The pose** the camera worked out.
2) **The time the picture was taken**, not the time now. A camera picture is a little old by the time it arrives, so the estimator needs to know how old and rewinds to put it in the right place. Using the time now would pin the picture to the wrong moment.
3) **How far off it could be**: a number of meters for x, another for y, and a number of radians for the heading. Small numbers mean "I trust this camera", big numbers mean "be careful". A far tag is less sure, so these grow with the tag's distance squared.

The loop variable `solution` already holds the pose and the time, and `tag_distance` holds the distance in meters to the closest tag it saw.
say.bit: The call takes the camera's pose, when the picture was TAKEN (not now), and how far off it could be (x and y meters, heading radians, bigger for far tags).

steps.title: How much to trust the cameras

say.never:
The third thing you pass is a **standard deviation**: how far off the camera could be. The estimator blends the cameras with odometry using it.

The two vision numbers in `LocalizationConstants` start very large, which says "the camera could be 5 meters off at 1 meter", so the estimator hardly listens. Make them smaller and it starts to follow the cameras.

Too large and the cameras are ignored. Too small and a bad camera reading is believed, so the estimate **jumps** around. The sweet spot is a number that matches how good your cameras really are: pick one, test it, and adjust.
say.bit: The vision numbers start huge, so the cameras are ignored. Too small and bad readings make the estimate jump. Pick a sensible number and test it.

say.never:
In the simulator there are no real cameras. A provided piece plays the camera computers and sends tag solutions into MW-Lib's **proxy server**, the same place real camera computers send theirs. In **AdvantageScope** you will look at three things:

- **Proxy/TagSolutions**: what the proxy server holds. Each solution has a pose, the time of its picture, the camera and the ids of the tags the camera saw. The pose comes from just the best one of them, and it gets worse the farther that tag is.
- **PositionErrorMeters**: how far your estimate is from the real position, in meters. Closer to zero is better.
- **The 2D Field**: your estimate (**Localization/Pose**) next to where the robot really is (**Drive/TruePose**). When vision works the two robots sit on top of each other.
say.bit: Look at three things in AdvantageScope: the tag solutions, PositionErrorMeters (closer to 0 is better), and the estimated robot against the true one on the 2D Field.

say.never:
Look at the error plot. While you drive it jumps around a little (up to about 0.2 meters). Once you stopped it should settle to a centimeter or two, well under the 6 cm limit.

If it stays large, the cameras are being ignored (numbers too big) or something in the call is wrong. If the estimate jumps around a lot even when you are standing still, the numbers are too small and a bad reading is being believed.
say.bit: The error should settle to a centimeter or two once you stop. If not, the trust numbers or the call are off.
